Anyone who has these words can read what you copy. Keep this page somewhere safe.

Clipway is a clipboard shared between a Mac and an Android phone, end-to-end encrypted. Its key is the 12 words on the first page; a copy may also be in the owner's password manager under the name Clipway.
The items pass through the relay %1$s and are erased from it after 24 hours at most. Nothing is kept in a cloud.
The history on each device is encrypted. If the owner exported it, the export is a ZIP file: history.json opens in any text editor (or with jq), and the images are in the items folder.
To read the key or the history, install Clipway, choose Pair, and type the 12 words.
No account. No tracking. No ads.
Nothing leaves your device unless you choose it.
The code will be published, so anyone can check this.

Deletes the key, the history and the settings on this phone. Files in Downloads stay.
This phone forgets the key, the history and the settings, and Clipway starts over. This cannot be undone. Files saved in Downloads stay.
Also erase the key on the relay
Unpairs your Mac too and deletes what waits on the relay. Without network, the relay erases it within 24 hours.

Texts you send with the tile, Send to Mac in the text menu, the share menu or Send clipboard, 64 KB at most. Never on their own: Android does not let apps read the clipboard in the background. Sent to the relay %1$s, end-to-end encrypted, with this phone\'s name inside.
Images and files: never on a server

They go straight from this phone to your Mac over your local network, encrypted with a key made for that one transfer. The relay only passes a short encrypted note that tells your Mac where to fetch it. So both devices need to be on the same network. Nobody can check what travels encrypted without an account, so our relay refuses to carry pictures or files at all.

Texts come from the relay %1$s, end-to-end encrypted. Images and files come straight from your Mac over your local network, encrypted with a key made for that one transfer. Only your devices hold the key.

A random chain id, the time and size of each item, how many of your devices are connected, and your IP address while connected. Never the content, file names, device names, or whether an item is a text or a note about a file.

Items wait on the relay for a device that is offline, 24 hours at most, in memory only. Then they are erased. The relay never logs your IP address. On clip.sidali.dev, the web server in front of it keeps IP addresses for 7 days.
Once a day, Clipway asks the relay %1$s if it is up and which app versions it accepts. No key and no content, only the app\'s name and version.
What apps mark as sensitive, like a password copied from your password manager.

Pair nearby uses Bluetooth only while you pair; no location is collected. Your Mac shows that it is pairing for 2 minutes at most, while its Pair nearby window is open, and sends the key to this phone over Bluetooth, encrypted, only after you press Pair on both. During those 2 minutes, devices in Bluetooth range can see that a Clipway Mac is pairing and read its Bluetooth name. Nothing about it is stored.
Never sent to the relay. It only goes to your password manager when you choose Save, and on paper when you print the rescue kit.
The key, encrypted by Android\'s keystore.
History: the last 50 items, encrypted. Erase everything destroys its key.
Received files, in Downloads/Clipway. They are yours.
While it sends an image or a file, for 2 minutes at most, this phone accepts one connection from your Mac on the local network. Without the key, a connection gets nothing.
Nothing goes into backups or device transfers.
Nothing else. No account, no analytics, no crash reports, no third-party services.
